vectorSources.name: Overture Maps buildings
vectorSources.description: Overture's buildings theme, worldwide: OpenStreetMap footprints first, then Esri Community Maps, Google Open Buildings and Microsoft's ML footprints where OSM has none, each feature naming its origin. Heights and floor counts where a source gives one (dense in North America, sparse elsewhere), with building parts for 3D. One PMTiles archive per monthly release, zoom 5 to 14; the app reads the current release from Overture's catalog. Tiles are heavy in dense cities (about 1 MB at zoom 14).
vectorSources.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation, Microsoft, Google, Esri Community Maps contributors

vectorSources.name: VIDA Google + Microsoft + OSM open buildings
vectorSources.description: 2.7 billion footprints merged per country by VIDA from Google Open Buildings V3, Microsoft's Global ML Building Footprints and OpenStreetMap (2024 snapshots): the widest coverage of Africa, South Asia and Latin America, where Google's footprints fill what OSM and Microsoft miss. No heights. One fixed PMTiles archive on Source Cooperative, zoom 0 to 15.
vectorSources.attribution: VIDA; Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0), Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (ODbL), © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap buildings (OpenFreeMap)
vectorSources.description: OpenStreetMap's buildings from OpenFreeMap's weekly planet tiles (OpenMapTiles schema), with the rendering height OpenMapTiles derives from OSM's height and levels tags: light tiles, footprints only where mappers drew them. The same tiles feed the building shadows.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap roads and labels (OpenFreeMap Liberty)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of OpenFreeMap's Liberty style, without its fills: roads, railways, waterways, boundaries, place and street names over any basemap or relief, as a hybrid map does. Drawn with Liberty's own colors; only the opacity is yours.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap roads and labels (OpenFreeMap Bright)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of OpenFreeMap's Bright style (its fork of OpenMapTiles' OSM Bright), without its fills: roads cased in white and yellow, railways, waterways, boundaries, place and street names and points of interest over any basemap or relief. Drawn with Bright's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: BSD 3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (design), KlokanTech and OpenMapTiles contributors, derived from Mapbox Open Styles. Checked 2026-11-27: style, tiles, fonts and sprite answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap roads and labels, light grey (OpenFreeMap Positron)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of OpenFreeMap's Positron style (its fork of OpenMapTiles' Positron), without its fills: white and pale grey roads, grey names, no points of interest. The quietest of the set: made to sit under data, it reads best over a dark relief or a colored raster. Drawn with Positron's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: BSD 3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (design), KlokanTech and OpenMapTiles contributors, derived from CARTO's basemaps (Stamen and Paul Norman for CartoDB, CC BY 3.0). Checked 2026-11-27: style, tiles, fonts and sprite answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap roads and labels, dark (OpenFreeMap Dark)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of OpenFreeMap's Dark style (OpenMapTiles' Dark Matter, unmodified but for its fonts), without its fills: near-black roads and dark grey names with black halos, made for a dark map. Over a light basemap or a pale relief it gives dark linework; over imagery it is hard to read. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. OpenFreeMap serves it but does not list it on its quick start page and calls it not yet complete. Style: BSD 3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (design), MapTiler and OpenMapTiles contributors, derived from CARTO's basemaps (CC BY 3.0). Checked 2026-11-27: style, tiles, fonts and sprite answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: OpenStreetMap roads and labels, blue-grey (OpenFreeMap Fiord)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of OpenFreeMap's Fiord style (OpenMapTiles' Fiord Color, unmodified but for its fonts), without its fills: slate-blue roads and pale blue names with dark blue halos, made for a dark blue map. Readable over imagery and dark relief. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. OpenFreeMap serves it but does not list it on its quick start page and calls it not yet complete. Style: BSD 3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (design), MapTiler and OpenMapTiles contributors, derived from CARTO's basemaps (CC BY 3.0). Checked 2026-11-27: style, tiles, fonts and sprite answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: Roads and labels for imagery (gpx.studio Liberty Satellite)
vectorSources.description: gpx.studio's Liberty Satellite: OpenFreeMap's Liberty reworked by gpx.studio to sit over imagery, with the fills and the road casings taken out, the roads made translucent, white names with dark halos, cased boundaries, and peaks, saddles and nature parks named. Drawn whole (lines, labels and one pattern on pedestrian squares): it was made as an overlay. The copy is served by this app (the licence allows it, with credit) and reads OpenFreeMap's tiles, fonts and sprite instead of gpx.studio's own hosts (same OpenMapTiles schema, same Noto Sans, same sprite), which answer no other site; the MapTiler satellite layer under it (a key) is left out, any basemap of the app takes its place. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: MIT (OpenFreeMap Styles, Zsolt Ero; gpx.studio), from OSM Liberty and OSM Bright (BSD 3-Clause code, CC BY 4.0 design). Checked 2026-11-27.
vectorSources.attribution: Style: gpx.studio (https://gpx.studio, https://github.com/gpxstudio/styles). OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: Roads, trails and labels (gpx.studio Liberty Topo)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of gpx.studio's Liberty Topo, without its fills: OpenFreeMap's Liberty with what a hiker reads added by gpx.studio, trails apart from paved footpaths, peaks and saddles with their heights, nature parks named. The original also draws a hillshade and contour lines in metres and feet from gpx.studio's own vector tiles (made from Mapterhorn), which answer no other site: they are left out, the app's own hillshade and contours do that over any terrain source. The copy is served by this app (the licence allows it, with credit) and reads OpenFreeMap's tiles, fonts and sprite. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: MIT (OpenFreeMap Styles, Zsolt Ero; gpx.studio), from OSM Liberty and OSM Bright (BSD 3-Clause code, CC BY 4.0 design), some layers from nst-guide's osm-liberty-topo. Checked 2026-11-27.
vectorSources.attribution: Style: gpx.studio (https://gpx.studio, https://github.com/gpxstudio/styles). OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: Roads and labels in the OpenStreetMap look (gpx.studio OSM)
vectorSources.description: The lines and labels of the OSM style gpx.studio serves (OpenMapTiles' rendition of openstreetmap.org's standard map), without its fills: red motorways, orange and yellow main roads, dashed paths and tracks, the standard map's icons and shields. The densest of the road overlays, with points of interest from zoom 14. The copy is served by this app (the licence allows it, with credit) and reads OpenFreeMap's tiles and fonts; its icons (287 small images, the 19 fill patterns left out) are served beside it. gpx.studio's OSM Topo is the same style with a hillshade and contour lines from its own tiles, which answer no other site: with those left out the two are one, so there is one entry. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: BSD 3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (design), OpenMapTiles contributors; icons from openstreetmap-carto (CC0). Checked 2026-11-27.
vectorSources.attribution: Style: gpx.studio (https://gpx.studio, https://github.com/gpxstudio/styles). OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: IGN roads and place names for aerial photographs (Carte Facile)
vectorSources.description: Carte Facile's aerial style without its photographs: the roads, railways, and the names of places, roads, rivers and summits that IGN's cartes.gouv.fr team lays over aerial imagery, from the Plan IGN vector tiles (France and its overseas territories, to zoom 18). Drawn whole, lines and labels: it was made as an overlay. Carte Facile keeps its styles inside an npm package, so a copy is served by this app, with its fonts (the same three Noto Sans) read from OpenFreeMap. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Style: Apache-2.0, La Fabrique des géocommuns (IGN). Tiles: © IGN, Licence Ouverte 2.0. Checked 2026-11-27: tiles answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: Style: Carte Facile (https://github.com/fab-geocommuns/carte-facile), Apache-2.0. Tiles © IGN, Plan IGN, Géoplateforme

vectorSources.name: swisstopo labels (Light Base Map)
vectorSources.description: The labels of swisstopo's Light Base Map, without its lines and fills: places, peaks and passes with their heights, lakes, rivers, glaciers, massifs, road numbers and stations, in swisstopo's own lettering (Frutiger Neue, served by swisstopo) and with its own symbols. swisstopo offers the service to everyone within Switzerland and Liechtenstein; the part of the map beyond is reserved to the Federal Administration, so the overlay is for those two countries. Drawn with the style's own colors; only the opacity is yours. Free geodata terms (OGD): the source must be named; in the event of excessive use, swisstopo may restrict access. Checked 2026-11-27: style, tiles, fonts and sprite answer with CORS, no key.
vectorSources.attribution: © swisstopo (Federal Office of Topography), Light Base Map; © OpenMapTiles, © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: HW.ai Heritage Map - OSM
vectorSources.description: Heritage Watch AI's weekly OpenStreetMap export: 4.46 million objects tagged historic=*, heritage=*, places of worship, museums, and other worship buildings, ruins and lighthouses, as points with their footprints from a second archive. The destroyed ones carry their lifecycle status.
vectorSources.attribution: Heritage Watch AI (Iconem), © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: HW.ai Heritage Map - Wikidata
vectorSources.description: Heritage Watch AI's weekly Wikidata export: 1.7 million items of 40 heritage classes (monuments, archaeological sites, places of worship, castles...) and 1.2 million more known by a heritage designation alone, as points. Colored by heritage class, the 40 classes in nine colors (an item of several classes takes the first of the legend's order), the ones Wikidata marks as gone in red. Properties: label, class list, designation, image, Wikidata id.
vectorSources.attribution: Heritage Watch AI (Iconem), data from Wikidata

vectorSources.name: OSM destroyed and disappeared features (HW.ai)
vectorSources.description: Every object OpenStreetMap marks with a lifecycle prefix (destroyed:, damaged:, demolished:, razed:, removed:, was:), of any kind and not only heritage: 663 thousand buildings, roads, amenities and historic features, with the date, event and type of damage where mappers gave one. Points and footprints in one archive, exported weekly by Heritage Watch AI for its Heritage map.
vectorSources.attribution: Heritage Watch AI (Iconem), © OpenStreetMap contributors

vectorSources.name: HW.ai Heritage Map - National and regional inventories
vectorSources.description: A compilation in progress of national and regional heritage inventories (monument registers, archaeological site records), one feature per record with its source, country, kind and licence class, as points with the footprints the inventories publish. The footprints are drawn as outlines, not fills: a register's perimeters run from a house to a reef or a whole landscape, and the archive has no size to tell them apart. Each inventory keeps its own licence: read the licence_class and url of a record before re-use.
vectorSources.attribution: Heritage Watch AI (Iconem), national and regional heritage inventories (each under its own licence)
vectorSources.licenseName: Per inventory (open, non-commercial or not stated)

vectorSources.name: UNESCO World Heritage List
vectorSources.description: The properties of UNESCO's World Heritage List (1,271 placed of 1,273), one point each, with category, year of inscription, States Parties, criteria, the List in Danger flag and a short description: a compact copy (0.65 MB) of the open data portal's dataset, which weighs 23 MB. A serial property stands on the component nearest to the middle of its parts; its parts are the companion source, World Heritage components.
vectorSources.attribution: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, World Heritage List (data.unesco.org, whc001), CC BY-SA 4.0

vectorSources.name: UNESCO World Heritage components (serial properties)
vectorSources.description: Every component of the 486 serial properties of the World Heritage List (those inscribed as several parts: the Aalto works, the Struve arc, the Frontiers of the Roman Empire), 5,612 points with the component's name and reference and the property it belongs to. From the components list of UNESCO's open data; 0.9 MB (155 KB once compressed by the server), a property's name and category said once for all its components.
vectorSources.attribution: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, World Heritage List (data.unesco.org, whc001), CC BY-SA 4.0

vectorSources.name: Overture Maps land cover
vectorSources.description: The land_cover layer of Overture's base theme, worldwide: polygons generalized from ESA WorldCover (10 m, 2020) into ten classes, a layer per zoom. Read from the theme's monthly PMTiles archive, which also holds water, bathymetry and infrastructure: its tiles weigh 2 to 4 MB below zoom 9 over Europe, so the layer is drawn from zoom 9 (0.2 to 1.6 MB a tile from there).
vectorSources.attribution: Overture Maps Foundation; ESA WorldCover (CC BY 4.0)

vectorSources.name: Overture Maps land use
vectorSources.description: The land_use layer of Overture's base theme, worldwide, from OpenStreetMap's landuse, leisure and amenity areas: 23 kinds grouped into ten colors, with the name and class of each area. The archive carries the classes at its deepest zoom only (13), so the layer is drawn from zoom 13; a tile of a dense city weighs up to 2 MB there (it also holds every tree and street lamp of the base theme), a rural one a few kilobytes.
vectorSources.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation

vectorSources.name: France - IGN OCS GE land cover 2021-2023 (vector)
vectorSources.description: IGN's large-scale land cover of France (OCS GE), the 2021 to 2023 vintage, as vector tiles of the Géoplateforme: 28 million polygons, each with its cover (14 classes, in the colors and under the names of IGN's own legend), its use and its year. OCS GE is produced department by department, about every three years, and the Géoplateforme serves one tile set per period: this one holds the departments surveyed in 2021, 2022 or 2023. Five were not (Rhône, Ille-et-Vilaine, Alpes-Maritimes, Gers and Var: their latest survey is of 2019 or 2020), so nothing draws over Lyon, Rennes, Nice, Auch or Toulon: use the 2017-2020 source there, which covers the whole of mainland France and Corsica. Zoom 13 to 16; a zoom 12 tile of Paris weighs 1.7 MB, so the layer is drawn from 13 (0.2 to 0.6 MB).
vectorSources.attribution: IGN, OCS GE (Occupation du sol à grande échelle), Licence Ouverte 2.0

Vector tiles of the Géoplateforme, zoom 13 to 16. The same five departments are missing (Rhône, Ille-et-Vilaine, Alpes-Maritimes, Gers and Var): use the 2017-2020 source there.

vectorSources.name: France - IGN OCS GE land cover 2017-2020 (vector)
vectorSources.description: The previous vintage of IGN's OCS GE land cover (surveys of 2017 to 2020), and the complete one: 29.9 million polygons over every department of mainland France and Corsica, including the five the 2021-2023 tile set lacks (Rhône, Ille-et-Vilaine, Alpes-Maritimes, Gers and Var; Lyon, Rennes, Nice and Toulon are of 2020, Auch of 2019). Same classes, colors and fields as the 2021-2023 source; where both exist, comparing them shows what changed in three years. Vector tiles of the Géoplateforme, drawn from zoom 13 to 16.
vectorSources.attribution: IGN, OCS GE (Occupation du sol à grande échelle), Licence Ouverte 2.0
